core_obligations: Reduce to a bijection on the spaces (proof lines 1166-1172): let X_0 and Y_0 be the sets of closed points; by assumption Y_0 maps bijectively onto X_0, and a w-local space is the disjoint union of the spectra of the local rings at its closed points, so X -> Y is a bijection.

Compare the localizations (proof lines 1172-1178): since A -> B is flat it satisfies going down, so for any prime q of B lying over a prime p of A the localization B_q equals B_p; by hypothesis B_q = A_p, whence A_p = B_p for every prime p of A.
Conclude (proof lines 1178-1181): a ring map which induces isomorphisms after localizing at every prime is an isomorphism, so A -> B is an isomorphism as claimed.
proof_roadmap: Use the bijection on closed points and the decomposition of w-local spaces to get a bijection on the spaces.
Use flatness and going down to identify the localizations of B at the primes over a given prime with B_p, and invoke the hypothesis that local rings are identified.
Conclude by the local criterion for a ring map to be an isomorphism.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that a ring map which identifies local rings, whose source and target spectra are w-local and w-local over each other, and which is bijective on the spaces of connected components, is an isomorphism (statement lines 1154-1164). The proof (proof lines 1166-1182) uses the decomposition of w-local spaces into the spectra of the local rings at closed points to get a bijection on spaces, uses flatness and going down to compare the localizations, and concludes by the local criterion for isomorphisms. H2: a three-step argument with three inputs, written out in full.
